# Cenivoz

> Cenivoz makes a voice AI interviewer for auto dealers across the US and Canada. Every applicant is invited to a spoken first interview, taken by phone or in a web browser at an hour they pick, and the dealership's managers receive scores, a hiring recommendation, a transcript and the audio. People at the dealership make every hiring decision.

This file belongs to the Cenivoz profile page on GitHub (https://cenivoz.github.io/). The official website is https://www.cenivoz.com, which keeps its own, fuller guide for AI assistants at https://www.cenivoz.com/llms.txt.

## Facts

- Category: voice AI interviewing and applicant screening, sold as browser-based software.
- Made for: franchise and independent car dealers, multi-store groups, and their service, parts and body-shop teams.
- Countries: United States and Canada.
- The interview: spoken, roughly 15 minutes long, held in English or Spanish. By phone (the interviewer calls at the slot the applicant picked) or in any web browser, any hour of any day.
- Jobs covered: technicians, service advisors, salespeople, BDC agents, parts staff, body-shop techs, finance managers and office staff, with other jobs on request.
- Report per interview: an overall score, five sub-scores (Communication, Technical, Problem Solving, Confidence, Behavior), a hiring recommendation ranging from Strong Hire down to No Hire, strengths, concerns, a transcript and the audio.
- Connections: signed webhooks and a REST API for applicant tracking systems, careers sites and dealer management systems, or the Cenivoz web panel for teams without one.
- Data: US-hosted on AWS, encrypted in transit, kept apart for each dealership, never used for AI training and never sold.
- Pricing: monthly, per store, quoted rather than published; most dealers try it first in a 30-day pilot.
- Contact: hello@cenivoz.com, +1 (765) 302-2223.

## What Cenivoz does not do

- It does not choose who gets the job: its recommendation is advice, and managers make the call.
- It does not talk pay or promise anyone a job: those questions go back to the dealership's team.
- It does not ask about or score protected characteristics: questions and scoring stick to the job.
- It does not train AI models on customer or applicant data, and does not sell that data.
- It does not advertise openings or hunt for candidates: it interviews the applicants a dealership already gets.
- It does not need an app: applicants use a phone or a browser, and the dealer's team works in the browser too.
